scenario: Greeting someone for the first time
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Common in 'Qual é o seu nome?'.
Auxiliary verb, here in the form 'é'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá! Prazer, o meu nome é Ana.
dialogue.translation: Hello! Nice to meet you, my name is Ana.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Olá, Ana! Muito prazer. Eu sou o João.
dialogue.translation: Hello, Ana! Nice to meet you. I am João.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: De onde você é, João?
dialogue.translation: Where are you from, João?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sou de Portugal. E você?
dialogue.translation: I am from Portugal. And you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sou do Brasil. Bem-vindo!
dialogue.translation: I am from Brazil. Welcome!

scenario: Asking where something is in a store
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Onde está o leite?
dialogue.translation: Where is the milk?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Está ali, perto do pão.
dialogue.translation: It's there, near the bread.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mas não vejo aqui. Fica onde?
dialogue.translation: But I don't see it here. Where is it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Por aqui, ao lado da fruta.
dialogue.translation: This way, next to the fruit.

key_phrases.translation: Where is it? (Where is it located?)

scenario: Ordering a drink at a café
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: commonly used for wishes and orders

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Eu quero um café quente, por favor.
dialogue.translation: I would like a hot coffee, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Temos também água fria, se preferir.
dialogue.translation: We also have cold water, if you prefer.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mas eu quero beber algo quente.
dialogue.translation: But I want to drink something hot.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Então, um café para você. E para mim, água.
dialogue.translation: Then, a coffee for you. And for me, water.

key_phrases.translation: I would like a hot coffee
I want to drink something hot

scenario: Buying a ticket at a station
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Uma hora para Lisboa, por favor.
dialogue.translation: A ticket to Lisbon, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quer o bilhete para hoje ou para amanhã?
dialogue.translation: Do you want the ticket for today or for tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Para hoje, por favor.
dialogue.translation: For today, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Pode dar-me o dinheiro? São vinte euros.
dialogue.translation: Can you give me the money? That's twenty euros.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Aqui tem. Muito obrigado.
dialogue.translation: Here you go. Thank you very much.

key_phrases.phrase: Uma hora para Lisboa, por favor.

key_phrases.translation: Can you give me the money?

scenario: Checking in at a hotel reception
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

dialogue.speaker: A (Gast)
dialogue.text: Boa noite! Já cheguei ao hotel.
dialogue.translation: Good evening! I have already arrived at the hotel.

dialogue.speaker: B (Rezeption)
dialogue.text: Bem-vindo! Tem uma reserva até amanhã?
dialogue.translation: Welcome! Do you have a reservation until tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: A (Gast)
dialogue.text: Sim, só uma noite. O quarto é pequeno, mas bom.
dialogue.translation: Yes, just one night. The room is small but good.

dialogue.speaker: B (Rezeption)
dialogue.text: Aqui está a chave, porque o quarto fica no segundo andar.
dialogue.translation: Here is the key, because the room is on the second floor.

dialogue.speaker: A (Gast)
dialogue.text: Obrigado! Até amanhã.
dialogue.translation: Thank you! See you tomorrow.

scenario: Meeting a new neighbor
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: regular -ar verb; used for where someone lives
agrees in gender/number; here masculine singular
invariable; used in greetings like 'tudo bem?'
used by male speakers; female says 'obrigada'
note: 'também' was not in the avoid list, it is 'também' with accent

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá! Você mora aqui no prédio?
dialogue.translation: Hello! Do you live here in the building?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, sou o vizinho novo. Tudo bem?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I'm the new neighbor. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tudo bem, obrigado. Precisa de ajuda para carregar as coisas?
dialogue.translation: All good, thank you. Do you need help carrying things?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Agora não, mas obrigado. Talvez depois, se puder.
dialogue.translation: Not now, but thank you. Maybe later, if you can.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Então, até logo!
dialogue.translation: Well then, see you later!

scenario: Asking the time on the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Relative and interrogative pronoun, very common
Plural of 'hora', used for telling time
3rd person plural of 'ser' – used for telling time
Number, here used for the time
Colloquial for 'half hour' in time expressions
As a noun: afternoon; also adverb: late

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Que horas são, por favor?
dialogue.translation: What time is it, please?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: São seis e meia.
dialogue.translation: It's half past six.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E são dez para as cinco?
dialogue.translation: And is it ten to five?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Não, são seis e meia da tarde.
dialogue.translation: No, it's half past six in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Obrigado!
dialogue.translation: Thank you!

scenario: At the doctor for a basic checkup
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: form of address for a doctor

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bom dia, doutor. Como está?
dialogue.translation: Good morning, Doctor. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bom dia. Eu estou bem, mas o senhor está doente?
dialogue.translation: Good morning. I am well, but are you sick?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Não me sinto muito bem. Sinto dor aqui.
dialogue.translation: I don't feel very well. I feel pain here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Fale mais sobre isso. O médico vai ajudar.
dialogue.translation: Tell me more about it. The doctor will help.

scenario: Paying at a supermarket checkout
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bom dia! O total é dez euros.
dialogue.translation: Good morning! The total is ten euros.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Posso pagar com cartão ou dinheiro?
dialogue.translation: Can I pay by card or cash?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Com cartão ou dinheiro, sim. Qual é o preço final?
dialogue.translation: By card or cash, yes. What is the final price?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Vou comprar só isto. Aqui tem o dinheiro.
dialogue.translation: I'll just buy this. Here is the money.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Obrigado. Você recebe o troco agora.
dialogue.translation: Thank you. You receive the change now.

scenario: Calling a friend to make simple plans
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Used here for 'tem' (you have) and 'tenho' (I have), often in expressions like 'ter tempo' (to have time).
Often used with 'ter' (to have), e.g., 'tenho tempo' (I have time).
Very common verb, also used as a future auxiliary (e.g., 'vamos ir' - we will go).
Here in the sense of 'to watch a movie' or 'to meet'.
Used to form polite questions and wishes, e.g., 'queres?' (do you want?).
Can mean a physical place or a seat (e.g., at the cinema).
Emphatic, to express agreement or similarity.
Important for contrasts and restrictions in a conversation.
Common word for a place or the art form.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá! Tu tens tempo agora?
dialogue.translation: Hello! Do you have time now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, tenho. Por quê? Queres ir ao cinema?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I do. Why? Do you want to go to the cinema?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, mas há um problema: não sei que filme ver.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but there's a problem: I don't know which movie to watch.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Podemos ver um filme novo, e depois ir a um lugar para comer.
dialogue.translation: We can watch a new movie, and then go to a place to eat.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Boa ideia! E eu também quero isso.
dialogue.translation: Good idea! And I want that too.

scenario: Describing your family to someone
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Feminine noun; in Brazil often pronounced with an open 'i'.
Often used for 'to live' (reside), similar to 'morar'.
Adverb; can also be an adjective (joined).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá! Como é a tua família?
dialogue.translation: Hello! What is your family like?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: A minha família é pequena: o meu pai, a minha mãe, o meu irmão e eu.
dialogue.translation: My family is small: my father, my mother, my brother, and me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tens irmãs ou só um irmão?
dialogue.translation: Do you have sisters or only one brother?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Só tenho um irmão, mas também tenho uma filha e um filho.
dialogue.translation: I only have one brother, but I also have a daughter and a son.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E vocês vivem juntos?
dialogue.translation: And do you live together?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, vivemos juntos. A minha filha chama-se Ana.
dialogue.translation: Yes, we live together. My daughter is named Ana.

scenario: Asking for directions in the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.translation: to be located, to be situated

vocabulary.note: With 'de' + place: 'longe daqui' = far from here
Common adverb, also used in directions

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Com licença, onde fica o banco?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where is the bank?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: É longe, mas não muito. Siga sempre em frente até a primeira rua.
dialogue.translation: It's far, but not very. Go straight ahead until the first street.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Então viro à direita ou à esquerda?
dialogue.translation: Then do I turn right or left?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Vire à esquerda. O banco fica perto do supermercado.
dialogue.translation: Turn left. The bank is near the supermarket.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Muito obrigado! Primeiro, esquerda, e depois perto do supermercado. Entendi.
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much! First left, then near the supermarket. Got it.

scenario: On a bus asking the driver for help
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Polite form of address for a man

vocabulary.translation: to get off, to go down

dialogue.speaker: A (Passagier)
dialogue.text: Senhor, pode me ajudar? Eu preciso saber se esta é a próxima estação.
dialogue.translation: Mister, can you help me? I need to know if this is the next station.

dialogue.speaker: B (Busfahrer)
dialogue.text: Sim, esta é a próxima estação. Mas você precisa descer já?
dialogue.translation: Yes, this is the next station. But do you need to get off now?

dialogue.speaker: A (Passagier)
dialogue.text: Sim, eu não quero perder a estação. Pode parar aqui?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I don't want to miss the station. Can you stop here?

dialogue.speaker: B (Busfahrer)
dialogue.text: Claro, eu paro já. Desça com cuidado.
dialogue.translation: Of course, I'll stop now. Get off carefully.

scenario: Introducing a colleague at work
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: comes after the noun: o colega novo
with preposition a: começar a trabalhar
here as adverb: muito prazer = very pleased
in greeting: muito prazer = very pleased

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, Maria! Quero apresentar-te o nosso novo colega, João.
dialogue.translation: Hello Maria! I want to introduce you to our new colleague, João.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Olá, João! Muito prazer. Onde trabalhas?
dialogue.translation: Hello João! Very pleased. Where do you work?

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Prazer, Maria. Eu trabalho na empresa ABC. Comecei hoje.
dialogue.translation: Pleased to meet you, Maria. I work at the company ABC. I started today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bem-vindo! Eu também trabalho lá.
dialogue.translation: Welcome! I also work there.

scenario: Leaving a voicemail message
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Also means 'to call' in context: falar com alguém.
Also reflexive: encontrar-se = to meet each other.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, aqui é a Ana. Você não está, então eu vou deixar uma mensagem.
dialogue.translation: Hello, this is Ana. You are not there, so I will leave a message.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, fale! Eu estou ouvindo.
dialogue.translation: Yes, speak! I am listening.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Eu quero falar com você sobre o nosso encontro. Por favor, me liga depois.
dialogue.translation: I want to talk to you about our meeting. Please call me later.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Qual é o seu número de telefone?
dialogue.translation: What is your phone number?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: É o nove, um, dois, três, quatro, cinco. Porque eu não estou em casa, liga para o meu celular.
dialogue.translation: It is nine, one, two, three, four, five. Because I am not at home, call my cell phone.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Está bem, eu vou encontrar você amanhã, então.
dialogue.translation: Okay, I will meet you tomorrow then.

scenario: At the post office sending a package
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Used to indicate purpose or recipient.
Here in 'por favor' (please) and 'por correio' (by mail).
Often used in questions about price/quantity.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bom dia! Eu quero enviar uma carta para a Alemanha.
dialogue.translation: Good morning! I want to send a letter to Germany.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro. E também um pacote? Ou só a carta?
dialogue.translation: Of course. And also a package? Or just the letter?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Só a carta. Quanto custa por correio normal?
dialogue.translation: Just the letter. How much does it cost by regular mail?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: O custo é cinco euros. A carta chega aqui em três dias.
dialogue.translation: The cost is five euros. The letter arrives here in three days.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Perfeito. Eu pago agora. E quando o meu amigo recebe a carta?
dialogue.translation: Perfect. I'll pay now. And when does my friend receive the letter?

scenario: Describing your daily routine
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: e.g. 'tomar café da manhã' (to have breakfast)

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: De manhã, eu acordo às seis horas e levanto-me.
dialogue.translation: In the morning, I wake up at six o'clock and get up.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Eu tomo o pequeno-almoço em casa e depois vou para o trabalho.
dialogue.translation: I have breakfast at home and then go to work.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: A que horas você almoça?
dialogue.translation: What time do you have lunch?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Almoço ao meio-dia, e à noite volto para casa e durmo cedo.
dialogue.translation: I have lunch at noon, and in the evening I return home and sleep early.

key_phrases.translation: to wake up at six o'clock

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Participle of 'abrir', often used as an adjective
Plural of 'hora', here used for time

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Olá, pode dizer-me que horas abre a loja?
dialogue.translation: Hello, can you tell me what time the store opens?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Abrimos às nove horas. Mas fechamos cedo na sexta-feira.
dialogue.translation: We open at nine o'clock. But we close early on Friday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E está aberto por todo o dia?
dialogue.translation: And is it open all day?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sim, mas fechamos para almoço. E ao sábado fechamos mais tarde.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but we close for lunch. And on Saturdays we close later.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Então, está aberto até às oito?
dialogue.translation: So, is it open until eight?

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Here used as emphasis in the order

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: O que você quer comer? O cardápio é bom.
dialogue.translation: What do you want to eat? The menu is good.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Quero o prato de peixe, mas sem cebola.
dialogue.translation: I want the fish dish, but without onions.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: E eu quero o mesmo, mas com arroz.
dialogue.translation: And I want the same, but with rice.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Você quer também uma sopa ou salada?
dialogue.translation: Do you also want a soup or salad?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Não, só o prato, obrigado.
dialogue.translation: No, just the dish, thank you.

key_phrases.translation: What do you want to eat?

key_phrases.phrase: Quero o prato de peixe, mas sem cebola.
key_phrases.translation: I want the fish dish, but without onions.

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of Portuguese

vocabulary.note: Polite form or informal address in Brazil
Irregular verb; also used for 'there is/are'
Irregular verb; often used for future (ir + infinitive)
Stem vowel change: eu quero, você quer

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Eu quero tirar dinheiro, mas não tenho a minha conta aqui.
dialogue.translation: I want to withdraw money, but I don't have my account here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Você pode ir ao caixa eletrônico com o seu cartão.
dialogue.translation: You can go to the ATM with your card.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Já fui, mas não funcionou.
dialogue.translation: I already went, but it didn't work.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Então, você quer falar com o gerente?
dialogue.translation: So, do you want to speak with the manager?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sim, eu quero resolver isso agora.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I want to resolve this now.
